messages:
Sean Gallagher: pulling follow-ups from yesterday’s tail-latency blip (Hosted canary + a couple Dedicated H100 pools). This thread = action items only (metrics/gates/docs). Please reply with what you’re taking + target date.

Context (tl;dr): profile tweak increased batching aggressiveness under mixed prefill/decode -> p99/p999 moved before we had a clean “queueing vs compute” signal. Rollback was fast but diagnosis took too long.

Top buckets to fix:
1) add missing metrics + tags
2) tighten perf-canary / rollout gates (esp mixed workloads)
3) update expected-behavior docs + runbook with the signals we actually used

Incident Bot: :memo: Post-incident follow-ups thread created. Owner: @sean.g. Related: INC-7713 (internal), PR-24988 (revert batching default).

Rafael Mendes: +1. For gates: we should treat “mixed workload p99 regression > X%” as a hard block, not warn. Right now perf-canary flags but doesn’t fail the train if error budget looks ok.

Allison Grant: metrics gap was the big one. We had latency histograms tagged with profile_id, but couldn’t separate scheduler queueing from GPU compute until we pulled traces manually.
Action item: add dashboard panels + alerts for `scheduler_queue_ms` by (sku, profile_id, workload_bucket). I can do dashboard + alert tuning this week.

Sofia Ivanova: I’ll take the runtime side for scheduler instrumentation improvements (separate `queue_ms` vs `compute_ms`, plus `admission_reject_count`). We already have PR-25063 in flight but it needs a follow-up to tag by `workload_bucket` consistently.
Target: end of week for PR + behind flag.

Omar El-Sayed: KV/cache signals were also missing for “why did decode get worse”. We need lightweight counters for:
- `kv_cache_compaction_ms` (already)
- `kv_cache_compaction_count`
- `allocator_fragmentation_estimate` (gauge)
- `oom_prevented_count` / `oom_kill_count`
I’ll sync with Samir but I can open a Linear + draft the metrics names/labels today.

Lena Fischer: from batching/backpressure: we need to surface the *effective* batch size / max tokens in flight per request class. Otherwise we’re arguing over config values vs what scheduler actually did.
Proposal metrics:
- `scheduler_inflight_tokens` (gauge)
- `scheduler_batch_size_prefill` / `scheduler_batch_size_decode` (hist)
- `scheduler_prefill_queue_depth` / `scheduler_decode_queue_depth`
I can wire the runtime emissions if Caleb ok’s the cardinality.

Caleb Johnson: re: cardinality — ok with those if we keep labels tight. Please no per-model labels on high-frequency histograms; we can do model-family bucket or “topN” sampling.
If we standardize on labels: `sku`, `profile_id`, `workload_bucket`, `deployment_mode` that’s fine.

Marcus Reed: for perf-canary gating, we should add a “mixed” workload suite that mirrors prod distribution (short prompts + long prompts + streaming) and make it required for default-profile changes.
I’ll update perf-canary config proposal:
- hard fail if p99 latency delta > 7% on mixed suite (per SKU)
- warn if p50 delta > 5% (informational)
- hard fail if error rate / timeouts > 1.2x baseline
Need buy-in on thresholds.

Claire Dubois: +1. Also we should pin random seeds + run ordering for mixed suite; yesterday’s first run was noisy and slowed decision-making.
I can add to benchmark protocol doc: “mixed suite requires 3 runs; take median; abort if variance > threshold”.

Jonas Weber: quantization note: the regression was amplified on int8 variant because decode is already near the edge on that profile; we should ensure mixed suite includes at least one quantized model.
Not asking to broaden model set a lot, just 1 representative.

Quentin Harris: docs + versioning: expected behavior pages need to call out “what changed in v1.0.3 vs v1.0.2” style. Otherwise SRE can’t map observed behavior to profile version quickly.
I’ll add a small “Known changes by profile_version” section template for each SKU page.

Connor O'Brien: release-process follow-up: any profile-default change must include:
- perf-canary link (run id)
- dashboard screenshot(s) or link with before/after
- explicit rollback instruction (kill switch vs pinning)
We can codify in the runtime-1.22 checklist. I’ll update the checklist + ask that it blocks go/no-go.

Mateo Alvarez: please make sure we don’t overcorrect by blocking too much. The gating should be strict on p99/p999 *only* for mixed suite + on SKUs where we’ve seen sensitivity.
Also: we need “fast rollback semantics”: revert just profile defaults without code deploy.
Rafael/Connor: let’s ensure the train includes a tested config-only rollback path.

Rafael Mendes: ack. We have the kill-switch for Hosted canary, but Dedicated needs a clearer “pin profile_version” playbook.
Action item: I’ll update the runbook section with exact steps:
- how to identify active profile_version from /health
- how to pin via control plane override
- how to validate rollback succeeded (dash panels)
Target: early next week.

Allison Grant: on alerts: we should page on sustained `kernel_fallback_rate` only if it correlates w/ p95+ regression. Otherwise it’s noise during ramp.
I’ll tune alerts to:
- ticket if fallback_rate > 2% for 10m
- page if fallback_rate > 5% AND p95 or scheduler_queue_ms above guardrail

Sofia Ivanova: for docs: I’ll update “Expected behavior – H100” with a troubleshooting table:
Symptom -> likely cause -> metrics to check -> mitigations
Example rows:
- p99 spikes + queue_ms up -> batching/admission limits
- p99 spikes + compute_ms up -> kernel fallback / KV compaction
- OOMs / restarts -> headroom too low / fragmentation

Omar El-Sayed: +1, and include the “normal ranges” for compaction time and fragmentation estimate per profile. Right now we just say “watch for increases” which isn’t actionable.

Lena Fischer: re: thresholds — can we add a “backpressure engaged” counter so we can tell if the system is protecting itself vs failing open?
Metric: `scheduler_backpressure_events_total` (counter), plus maybe `scheduler_backpressure_active` (gauge).

Caleb Johnson: yes. Keep event rate low; counter is fine.

Marcus Reed: I’ll propose initial thresholds in perf-canary PR:
- Mixed suite p99: fail if > +7% vs baseline (per SKU)
- scheduler_queue_ms p95: fail if > +10% (since that’s where “silent regressions” showed)
- throughput tokens/sec: warn only (since we care more about latency in canary)
We can adjust after a week of data.

Connor O'Brien: please link the incident + the revert PR in any gating change PR description. Release reviewers will ask.

Sean Gallagher: great. Quick roll-up (reply if I missed you):
- Allison: dashboard panels + alert tuning for scheduler_queue_ms + fallback correlation (this week)
- Sofia: instrumentation + docs troubleshooting table + workload_bucket tagging (end of week)
- Omar (+Samir): KV/cache + fragmentation metrics + normal ranges to docs (open ticket today)
- Lena (+Caleb): effective batching / inflight tokens + backpressure metrics (PR next week)
- Marcus (+Claire/Jonas): mixed workload suite + deterministic runs + include 1 quant model + gating thresholds (this week)
- Quentin: expected behavior doc template adds “Known changes by profile_version” (this week)
- Connor: release checklist updates to require perf-canary + rollback steps (today/tomorrow)
- Rafael: Dedicated pin/rollback runbook updates (early next week)

Please drop links to the Linear issues/PRs when created so we can track.

Allison Grant: created dashboard stub: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/runtime-profiles (WIP)
Will add panels once Sofia’s tags land. [reaction: :eyes: from Sean Gallagher]

Connor O'Brien: checklist PR opened (draft): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/25091
Adds required fields for “profile defaults change” section. [reaction: :thumbsup: from Mateo Alvarez]

Omar El-Sayed: Linear filed for KV/cache + fragmentation metrics: ENG-4988
Also adding doc TODOs to expected-behavior pages. [reaction: :white_check_mark: from Sean Gallagher]

Marcus Reed: perf-canary change request drafted: PERF-412 (mixed suite + hard gate). Will post PR link once up.

Sean Gallagher: closing loop: next postmortem review meeting we’ll confirm these shipped + validate alert noise. If anything slips, call it out here so it doesn’t disappear.
